mechanism: Bumetanide causes electrolyte depletion and hypokalemia while oxybutynin has anticholinergic effects that can exacerbate urinary retention and electrolyte imbalances, creating additive adverse effects.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes regularly, particularly potassium levels; assess for signs of urinary retention and dehydration; consider alternative anticholinergic or ensure adequate fluid and electrolyte replacement.
